title: Neuron
think_prompt: The nervous system carries information rapidly. What specialised cell makes this possible?
definition: A neuron, or nerve cell, is the structural unit of the nervous system and is specialised to transmit impulses.
description: This subunit introduces the neuron, its main parts, how structure supports function, and the three functional types of neurons: sensory, motor and interneurons.
key_points: Structural unit|Specialised cell|Transmits impulses|Sensory neuron|Motor neuron|Interneuron
image_description: 16:9 Grade 11 biology overview illustration showing one large scientifically clear typical neuron across the frame. Include dendrites, cell body with nucleus, a long axon, myelin sheath segments, nodes of Ranvier and terminal branches. Use a subtle directional arrow to suggest impulse travel, but keep labels minimal because detailed labelling is taught in the next scene. Clean textbook-quality scientific style, suitable for a classroom smart board.
interaction_instruction: Ask students to observe the overall shape of the neuron and predict why it is suited for carrying information.
quick_check: What is the structural unit of the nervous system?

title: Main Parts of a Neuron
think_prompt: Which parts receive information, and which part carries it away from the cell body?
definition: A neuron is composed of a cell body and nerve fibres. The main nerve-fibre processes are dendrites and an axon.
description: The cell body contains the nucleus and other cell organelles. Dendrites are slender processes that receive stimuli or impulses and transmit them toward the cell body. A single axon arises from the cell body and carries impulses away from it.
image_description: 16:9 precise labelled diagram of a typical neuron. Clearly show and label dendrites, cell body, nucleus, axon, myelin sheath and nodes of Ranvier. Arrange the neuron horizontally so the whole cell is visible. Use thin scientific leader lines, large readable labels and a clean Grade 11 textbook style.
interaction_instruction: Ask students to identify the cell body, nucleus, dendrites and axon before revealing the labels.
quick_check: Name the main parts of a neuron.

title: Structure and Function
think_prompt: How does the structure of each part help information move through a neuron?
definition: The structure of a neuron is specialised for receiving and transmitting impulses.
description: Dendrites receive stimuli or impulses and transmit them toward the cell body. The axon transmits impulses away from the cell body. In most chordate neurons, the axon is covered by a myelin sheath interrupted at nodes of Ranvier. The myelin sheath increases the speed of impulse transmission.
key_points: Dendrites → toward cell body|Axon → away from cell body|Myelin sheath increases transmission speed|Nodes of Ranvier interrupt myelin sheath
image_description: 16:9 structure-function infographic using one typical neuron. Highlight dendrites with arrows moving toward the cell body, then one clear arrow along the axon moving away from the cell body. Show myelin sheath as separated segments and identify the gaps as nodes of Ranvier. Visually connect each structure to its function without advanced molecular detail. Clean scientific Grade 11 style.
interaction_instruction: Ask students to trace the direction of impulse movement through the neuron.
quick_check: How do dendrites and the axon differ in the direction they transmit impulses?
answer: Dendrites transmit impulses toward the cell body; the axon transmits impulses away from the cell body.

title: Sensory Neuron
think_prompt: Which neuron carries information from a sensory organ toward the central nervous system?
definition: A sensory neuron transmits impulses from sensory organs to the central nervous system.
description: The cell body of a sensory neuron lies along the nerve fibre and the cell bodies occur in a ganglion. The dendritic end is associated with the sensory organ, while the axon extends toward the central nervous system.
key_points: Sensory organ → CNS|Cell body along nerve fibre|Cell bodies in ganglion|Dendritic end at sensory organ|Axon toward CNS
image_description: 16:9 scientifically accurate simplified sensory-neuron diagram. Show a receptor or sensory organ on the left, a long fibre with the cell body positioned along the pathway, and the axon continuing toward a clearly marked CNS region on the right. Add a strong directional arrow from sensory organ to CNS. Keep the diagram clean and distinct from motor-neuron morphology.
interaction_instruction: Ask students to identify the direction of impulse transmission and the position of the cell body.
quick_check: What is the main function of a sensory neuron?
answer: To transmit impulses from sensory organs to the central nervous system.

title: Motor Neuron
think_prompt: Which neuron carries commands from the central nervous system to a muscle?
definition: A motor neuron transmits impulses from the central nervous system to an effector such as a muscle.
description: A motor neuron has a star-shaped cell body with many processes. One long process is the axon. The cell body and other fibres are found within the central nervous system, while the axon carries impulses toward the effector.
key_points: CNS → Effector|Star-shaped cell body|Long axon|Cell body in CNS|Carries impulses to muscles
image_description: 16:9 scientifically accurate motor-neuron diagram. Show a star-shaped cell body with many dendrites inside a simplified CNS region on the left, one long axon extending across the frame, and a skeletal muscle effector on the right. Add a directional arrow from CNS toward muscle. Use a clean Grade 11 biology style and emphasize the long axon.
interaction_instruction: Ask students to compare the position of the motor-neuron cell body with that of the sensory neuron.
quick_check: What is the main function of a motor neuron?
answer: To transmit impulses from the central nervous system to an effector.

title: Interneuron
think_prompt: Which neuron connects a sensory neuron with a motor neuron inside the central nervous system?
definition: An interneuron is a neuron located within the central nervous system that connects other neurons.
description: The whole interneuron is found within the central nervous system. It usually has many dendrites and a short axon. Its role is to connect sensory neurons with motor neurons.
key_points: Entirely within CNS|Short axon|Many dendrites|Connects sensory and motor neurons
image_description: 16:9 simplified interneuron illustration located completely inside a clearly marked CNS area. Show a compact neuron with many dendrites and a short axon positioned between an incoming sensory-neuron pathway and an outgoing motor-neuron pathway. Emphasize the linking role without drawing a full reflex arc or stimulus-response sequence.
interaction_instruction: Ask students to identify what two neuron types the interneuron can connect.
quick_check: Where is an interneuron found and what does it do?
answer: It is found within the central nervous system and connects sensory neurons with motor neurons.

title: Compare the Three Neuron Types
memory_badge: Same purpose: transmit impulses — different roles
think_prompt: How can sensory, motor and interneurons be distinguished by location, structure and direction of impulse transmission?
definition: Sensory, motor and interneurons are specialised for different roles in nervous coordination.
description: Compare the three neuron types using their main role, location of the cell body, characteristic structure and direction of impulse transmission.
key_points: Feature|Sensory neuron|Motor neuron|Interneuron;Main role|Sensory organ to CNS|CNS to effector|Connects neurons in CNS;Cell body|Along nerve fibre in ganglion|In CNS|In CNS;Axon|Toward CNS|Long axon toward effector|Short;Impulse direction|Sensory organ → CNS|CNS → effector|Within CNS
image_description: 16:9 comparison-table visual with three equal columns headed Sensory Neuron, Motor Neuron and Interneuron. Include a small accurate neuron sketch at the top of each column. Use rows for Main role, Cell-body position, Location, Axon characteristic and Direction of impulse. Keep wording concise, typography large, and the table clean enough for smart-board viewing.
interaction_instruction: Ask students to read across each row and identify one structural and one functional difference among the three neuron types.
quick_check: Which neuron carries impulses from the CNS to an effector?
remarks: Comparison scene intentionally designed as a table

title: Identify the Neuron Type
think_prompt: Can you identify a neuron type from where the impulse starts and where it goes?
definition: Neuron type can be identified by its location, structure and direction of impulse transmission.
description: Use simple pathway clues rather than a reflex-arc example. If an impulse travels from a sensory organ to the CNS, identify a sensory neuron. If it travels from the CNS to an effector, identify a motor neuron. If the neuron lies completely within the CNS and links other neurons, identify an interneuron.
key_points: Sensory organ → CNS = sensory neuron|CNS → effector = motor neuron|Within CNS linking neurons = interneuron
image_description: 16:9 three-case classification visual. Case A shows a pathway from a sensory organ toward the CNS. Case B shows a pathway from the CNS toward a muscle. Case C shows a short linking neuron entirely inside the CNS. Do not label the neuron types in the image; use A, B and C only so students must identify Sensory, Motor and Interneuron from the pathway clues. Avoid a complete reflex arc.
interaction_instruction: Ask students to identify neuron A, B and C and justify each answer using impulse direction or location.
quick_check: A neuron lies entirely within the CNS and links two other neurons. What type is it?

title: Neuron Recall Check
think_prompt: Can you describe a neuron without looking back at the previous scenes?
definition: A neuron is a specialised nerve cell that receives and transmits impulses.
description: Recall the main structural features of a neuron and distinguish sensory, motor and interneurons by their role and direction of impulse transmission. This scene consolidates SU03 without introducing the reflex arc.
key_points: Neuron = structural unit|Dendrites toward cell body|Axon away from cell body|Sensory → CNS|Motor → effector|Interneuron within CNS
image_description: 16:9 retrieval-practice visual showing a central simple neuron with unlabeled pointers to dendrites and axon, plus three small pathway clues representing sensory, motor and interneuron roles. Use question marks instead of answers so students must recall the terms. Clean, minimal Grade 11 classroom design.
interaction_instruction: Ask students to name the main parts and state the role of each neuron type without returning to earlier scenes.
quick_check: State one structural feature and one function of a neuron.
answer: A neuron has specialised processes such as dendrites and an axon; it receives and transmits impulses.
